title: pvPointLineInterpolator
body:
## pvPointLineInterpolator

Interpolates point data from a point cloud (Input) onto a high-resolution straight line set in the Source options (Point1, Point2, Resolution; ParaView default 1000 intervals), producing a polyline profile for line plots. Use it for profiles through scattered or particle data; for data on a mesh with cells, probeLine samples by cell interpolation instead.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The line endpoints may be derived by ParaView from the input bounds, but Schemaxis has not verified that; their static default is [0, 0, 0] for both, a degenerate line. Set Point1 and Point2 explicitly in dataset coordinates.
- Points with no cloud points inside the kernel footprint receive NullValue (0 by default, NullPointsStrategy "Null Value" per the XML default), which can look like real zeros; choose Mask Points to flag them.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `PointLineInterpolator`. Identity: `filters/PointLineInterpolator`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The data source to be interpolated onto the *Source*. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component. The input needs at least one point-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel` | Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel","Gaussian Kernel","Linear Kernel","Probabilistic Voronoi Kernel","Shepard Kernel","Voronoi Kernel"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel"}` |
| `Locator` | Specify a point locator. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Static Point Locator"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Static Point Locator"}` |
| `NullPointsStrategy` | How output points that have no source point in their neighbourhood (null points) get a value. Mask Points adds an output array that marks each point valid (1) or null (0) and also sets the NullValue; Null Value (ParaView's default, entry 1) writes the NullValue to null points; Closest Point uses the closest source point. ParaView's own text calls Closest Point the default, but its XML default is 1 (Null Value), as in vtkPointInterpolator. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Mask Points","Null Value","Closest Point"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Mask Points"` |
| `NullValue` | Specify the null point value. When a null point is encountered then all components of each null tuple are set to this value. By default the null value is set to zero. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `PassCellArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input cell data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassFieldArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input field data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassPointArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input point data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Source` | The data source that provides the structure to be interpolated on. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Line"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Line"}` |
| `ValidPointsMaskArrayName` | If the NullPointsStrategy is "Mask Points", then an array is generated for each input point. This vtkCharArray is placed into the output of the filter, with a non-zero value for a valid point, and zero otherwise. The name of this masking array is specified here. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/EllipsoidalGaussianKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.Eccentricity` | Shape of the ellipsoid relative to each point’s normal: 1 is spherical, values below 1 give a needle along the normal, values above 1 a pancake perpendicular to it. In the weight exp(−Sharpness² · (r⊥²/E² + z²)/R²) it divides the distance measured perpendicular to the normal. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |
| `Kernel.options.Radius` | Search radius R in dataset units: source points within it form the neighbourhood, and R also normalizes the distances in the Gaussian weight. If no source point lies within R, the operation’s NullPointsStrategy decides the result. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |
| `Kernel.options.Sharpness` | Fall-off of the Gaussian: larger values reduce the influence of distant neighbours (less smoothing), smaller values blend more evenly. | `{"minimum":1.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1.0` |
| `Kernel.options.UseNormals` | When true, each splat is oriented by the source point’s normal: VTK uses the source’s active normals, or else a point array named “Normals”. If neither exists, the kernel behaves as a spherical Gaussian. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Kernel.options.UseScalars` | When true, each neighbour’s weight is multiplied by its scalar value before normalization, so points with larger scalars dominate (useful for confidence values). VTK uses the source’s active scalars, or else a single-component array named “Scalars”. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Gaussian Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Gaussian Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/GaussianKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.KernelFootprint` | How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Radius","N Closest"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Radius"` |
| `Kernel.options.NumberOfPoints` | Number of nearest source points used for each sample when KernelFootprint is “N Closest”; ignored for “Radius”. Larger values blend over more points and smooth more. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Kernel.options.Radius` | Search radius R around each sample point, used when KernelFootprint is “Radius” (ignored for “N Closest”). It also sets the width of the Gaussian: weights are exp(−(Sharpness · r / R)²), so a larger R both gathers more points and smooths more. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |
| `Kernel.options.Sharpness` | Fall-off rate s of the Gaussian weights exp(−(s · r / R)²): larger values reduce the influence of more distant neighbours (less smoothing), smaller values blend more evenly across the neighbourhood. | `{"minimum":1.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1.0` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Linear Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Linear Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/LinearKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.KernelFootprint` | How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Radius","N Closest"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Radius"` |
| `Kernel.options.NumberOfPoints` | Number of nearest source points used for each sample when KernelFootprint is “N Closest”; ignored for “Radius”. Larger values blend over more points and smooth more. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Kernel.options.Radius` | Search radius around each sample point, used when KernelFootprint is “Radius” (ignored for “N Closest”). Every source point inside it receives the same weight, so a larger radius averages over a wider region. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Probabilistic Voronoi Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Probabilistic Voronoi Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/ProbabilisticVoronoiKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.KernelFootprint` | How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Radius","N Closest"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Radius"` |
| `Kernel.options.NumberOfPoints` | Number of nearest source points used for each sample when KernelFootprint is “N Closest”; ignored for “Radius”. Larger values blend over more points and smooth more. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Kernel.options.Radius` | Search radius around each sample point, used when KernelFootprint is “Radius” (ignored for “N Closest”). Only source points inside it are candidates for the closest point; if none lie inside, the sample is a null point. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Shepard Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Shepard Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/ShepardKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.KernelFootprint` | How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Radius","N Closest"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Radius"` |
| `Kernel.options.NumberOfPoints` | Number of nearest source points used for each sample when KernelFootprint is “N Closest”; ignored for “Radius”. Larger values blend over more points and smooth more. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Kernel.options.PowerParameter` | Exponent p in the weights 1/r^p. Larger p makes the nearest neighbours dominate (approaching nearest-neighbour behaviour); smaller p averages more evenly. p = 2 uses a fast squared-distance path; other values evaluate a power per neighbour and can be markedly slower. | `{"maximum":100.0,"minimum":0.001,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.001` |
| `Kernel.options.Radius` | Search radius around each sample point, used when KernelFootprint is “Radius” (ignored for “N Closest”). It only limits which neighbours take part; their weights depend on distance through PowerParameter, not on the radius. | `{"minimum":1e-06,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1e-06` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `Voronoi Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"Voronoi Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/VoronoiKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

No authored options.


### Nested `Locator` → `Static Point Locator`

Syntax: `{"type":"Static Point Locator","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_locators/StaticPointLocator`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Locator.options.Automatic` | When true, the locator derives its bucket grid from the number of source points and NumberOfPointsPerBucket; when false, it uses Divisions exactly. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Locator.options.Divisions` | Bucket counts [nx, ny, nz] along x, y and z, used only when Automatic is false. Very fine grids waste memory on sparse clouds; very coarse grids make each search scan many points. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Locator.options.NumberOfPointsPerBucket` | Average number of source points per bucket targeted when Automatic is true; smaller values create more, smaller buckets. Ignored when Automatic is false. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `Source` → `Line`

Syntax: `{"type":"Line","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `extended_sources/HighResLineSource`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Source.options.Point1` | Start point [x, y, z] of the line, in the input’s coordinates; the first seed or sample point lies exactly here. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Source.options.Point2` | End point [x, y, z] of the line, in the input’s coordinates; the last seed or sample point lies exactly here. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Source.options.Resolution` | Number of equal segments of the probe line; the line has Resolution + 1 sample points, each receiving interpolated values. Higher values give a finer profile along the line. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
